definition: Visual temporal attention is a special case of visual attention that involves directing attention to specific instant of time.
details: Similar to its spatial counterpart visual spatial attention, these attention modules have been widely implemented in video analytics in computer vision to provide enhanced performance and human interpretable explanation of deep learning models. As visual spatial attention mechanism allows human and/or computer vision systems to focus more on semantically more substantial regions in space, visual temporal attention modules enable machine learning algorithms to emphasize more on critical video frames in video analytics tasks, such as human action recognition. In convolutional neural network-based systems, the prioritization introduced by the attention mechanism is regularly implemented as a linear weighting layer with parameters determined by labeled training data.

explainer.lead: Visual temporal attention directs a model's attention to specific instants of time within video. It helps video models emphasise the frames that matter most.

tiers.eli5: Like watching a video and paying extra attention to the few seconds where something important happens, while skimming the rest.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add attention modules to video models to weight frames; a common pitfall is that the weighting must be learned well or the model misses brief but critical events.
tiers.paperLevel: A special case of visual attention directed at specific instants of time; like spatial attention, it is used in video analytics to improve performance and give human-interpretable explanations, though interpretability depends on the learned weights.

explainer.example: In a surveillance clip, the model weights the frames where a person enters the scene more heavily than the empty background frames.
